text: OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, and c-MYC first reprogrammed human somatic cells to pluripotency. Unlike in mouse, OCT4 substitution in human cells previously failed, but transcriptome/bioinformatic analysis identified lineage-specifier factors replacing OCT4 and SOX2 in human fibroblasts, supporting counteracting lineage-specification networks. HDAC inhibitor valproic acid boosted reprogramming efficiency over 100-fold (Oct4-GFP reporter) and enabled pluripotent stem cell induction without c-Myc. G-quadruplex (G4)-forming sequences, including telomeres, act as replication fork barriers; homologous recombination stabilizes/restarts stalled forks. G-rich telomeric repeat replication efficiency dropped significantly in HR-lacking cells, and G4-stabilizer pyridostatin increased telomere fragility in BRCA2-deficient cells, reducing proliferation via double-strand breaks, checkpoint activation, and deregulated G2/M—including olaparib-resistant cells (53BP1/REV7 loss). Psoralen-induced interstrand cross-links caused chromosome breakage and 4N delay only after S-phase; primary human fibroblasts removed ~2,500 ICLs/genome at ~11 ICLs/genome/h.
